Playbook.name: Change Audit — Windows User Account Created/Deleted/Enabled/Disabled/Modified - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A user account was created/enabled/deleted/disabled or modified (4720/4722/4725/4726/4738/4767/4781). This is the canonical account-lifecycle audit (the QA-AD Created/Deleted OR-variants duplicate it and are retiring). Triage question: authorised IAM lifecycle action, or an attacker creating a backdoor account or manipulating one?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Attacker-created or -modified accounts provide persistence and access; unexpected lifecycle changes on privileged accounts are high risk.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the account lifecycle change is authorised IAM activity or an unauthorised backdoor/manipulation.

Step.name: Reconstruct the account change and actor
Step.Purpose: Identify what changed on which account by whom, and whether several accounts were touched.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4720","4722","4725","4726","4738","4767","4781") AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS changes = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), targets = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY host.name | SORT changes DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: 4720 create + 4722 enable of a new account in minutes = account provisioning (or backdoor). A burst of changes across accounts by one actor is scripted. Suppression is per Subject+Target 1h.

Step.name: Was a newly created account then added to a group or used
Step.Purpose: A new account added to a privileged group or logging on immediately is a backdoor pattern.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4728","4732","4756","4624") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), groups = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Create -> add-to-privileged-group -> logon within minutes is a classic backdoor sequence. Empty = a plain account change.

Node.Condition: A new account created then added to a privileged group / used, by an unfamiliar actor with no ticket.
Modification/enable of a privileged account by an unexpected actor.
Known IAM admin performing lifecycle changes under an approved process.
Plausible admin, no ticket, no follow-on.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-ACCT-CHANGE, INV-02-ACCT-FOLLOWON to the case.

TruePositive.Definition: Backdoor account creation or account manipulation.

SOCAction.Item: Disable the account; open IR; review the actor.
Check for other backdoors by the same actor.

Indicators.Item: Provisioning account per a broken job.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
